checkpoint: Exclusive private payload ownership and core transfer admission
status: implemented in Rust only; native private-session entry remains unavailable
behavior: Inspection pins the chosen parent without creating payload folders.
Private adds/imports reject existing-file reuse and destinations other than the configured parent.
The first preparation creates a fresh owner-only session directory; every transfer receives a fresh exclusive child.
Private storage retains root/nested directory descriptors and original file-inode pins in memory.
Unknown paths require exclusive creation; reopened files must match retained identity, ownership, mode and single-link checks.
Quarantine is required before payload writes; no library metadata or resume records are written by this backend.
Initial partial-file selection uses index-only boundary storage instead of info-hash paths.
Later private file membership/priority changes, relocation, rename, recovery, durable settings and payload deletion remain blocked.
End, failed admission and removal without deletion retain created folders, selected payloads and hidden boundary bytes.
Resume/recheck reject replaced owned directory paths; existing file descriptors continue to refer to their original inodes.

limitations: This is a core API, not a user-facing private torrent-client mode.
Transient folder authority and the authenticated private helper remain to be implemented.
Directory creation/open races and same-user interference are not certified safe by compiler checks.
In-flight I/O on existing descriptors can continue on original moved inodes; no instantaneous pathname-change stop claim.
Each materialized file requires an additional retained descriptor; large-torrent and descriptor-exhaustion acceptance remains.
Opaque retained folders may require manual organization and verification for later ordinary-library reuse.
No anonymity, secure-erasure, crash-recovery or universal leak-prevention claim.
